Patient: I'm 60 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because I've been having numbness and tingling in both of my hands for a few weeks now. It started after my car wreck last December when I broke both my wrists. The symptoms have gotten worse over the last month, and I've also been having some mild stiffness in my neck.
Doctor: Could you describe the progression of the numbness and tingling in your hands? Have you noticed any associated pain, weakness, or changes in sensation in your arms or fingers? Additionally, could you provide more details about the neck stiffness, such as its duration, severity, and whether it is associated with any headaches, dizziness, or visual changes?
Patient: The numbness and tingling started after my car wreck last December when I broke both wrists. At first, I thought it was just part of the healing process, but once my wrists healed, the tingling and numbness became more noticeable. They’ve gotten worse over the last month. I also have some mild stiffness in my neck, which I hit during the accident, and they told me it was a contusion. The stiffness isn’t too bad, but it’s been there since the accident. I haven’t had any headaches, dizziness, or visual changes with it.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies for your neck or wrists since the accident, such as X-rays, MRI, or CT scans? If so, could you provide the results or details of those examinations?
Patient: I had a CT brain with and without contrast done on February 5th, and they said there was no metastatic disease or acute intercranial abnormalities. I don’t know about any imaging for my neck or wrists specifically.
Doctor: Could you describe the distribution of the numbness and tingling in your hands? Are there any specific patterns or areas that are more affected? Have you noticed any associated weakness or pain radiating from your neck or arms?
Patient: The numbness and tingling on my right hand is from my middle and ring finger all the way up to my forearm, and on my left hand, it's more on the pinky and ring finger, not the middle. I don't really feel pain with it, just some soreness and weakness, especially when I use my hands. Sometimes they throb, but the tingling is more of a dull feeling. I haven't noticed any pain radiating from my neck or arms, just the stiffness there.
Doctor: Has the patient undergone any imaging studies for the cervical spine or wrists since the car wreck? If not, would they be willing to undergo cervical spine imaging (e.g., MRI or X-ray) to evaluate for potential nerve compression or spinal involvement?
Patient: I don’t know about any imaging for my neck or wrists specifically. I had a CT brain with and without contrast done on February 5th, but that was for something else. I haven’t had any imaging for my neck or wrists since the accident.
Doctor: Could you describe any changes in the numbness and tingling over the past few weeks? For example, has it gotten worse, better, or stayed the same? Also, have you noticed any weakness or difficulty with fine motor tasks in your hands?
Patient: The numbness and tingling have gotten worse over the last month, especially in my right hand. I’ve noticed my hands feel weaker, especially when I’m using them, and it’s been harder to do things like button my shirt or hold small objects. The tingling comes and goes throughout the day, but it’s more noticeable at night.
